title: Compilation with an added memory tape
statement: Let $A$ assign memory-capable instructions to program nodes, let $l_0$ be an initial node, let $D$ be a Boolean-alphabet machine with $k_D$ work tapes and state set $SD$, and let $q_0$ assign an initial state of $D$ to each of $d$ decider indices. The compiled machine has $m+k_D+1$ work tapes and states that record a program node and phase together with the decider's simulation data. It starts at $(l_0,\mathrm{start})$; at each step it executes a memory instruction selected by the memory selector when one is available, and otherwise uses the compiled register-program and decider transition.
hypotheses_covered: A Boolean-alphabet machine $D$ with $k_D$ work tapes and states $SD$
caveat: The supplied snippet uses the constructions `mop`, `liftAct`, `ctr`, and `armProg` without giving their defining descriptions, so the transition rule can only be summarized at a high level.
